From 6abc7d5dcf0ee0f85e16e41c87fbd06231f28753 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Zilin Guan <zilin@seu.edu.cn>
Date: Mon, 26 Jan 2026 07:15:33 +0000
Subject: [PATCH] md/raid1: fix memory leak in raid1_run()

raid1_run() calls setup_conf() which registers a thread via
md_register_thread(). If raid1_set_limits() fails, the previously
registered thread is not unregistered, resulting in a memory leak
of the md_thread structure and the thread resource itself.

Add md_unregister_thread() to the error path to properly cleanup
the thread, which aligns with the error handling logic of other paths
in this function.

Compile tested only. Issue found using a prototype static analysis tool
and code review.

Link: https://lore.kernel.org/linux-raid/20260126071533.606263-1-zilin@seu.edu.cn
Fixes: 97894f7d3c29 ("md/raid1: use the atomic queue limit update APIs")
Signed-off-by: Zilin Guan <zilin@seu.edu.cn>
Reviewed-by: Li Nan <linan122@huawei.com>
Signed-off-by: Yu Kuai <yukuai@fnnas.com>

diff --git a/drivers/md/raid1.c b/drivers/md/raid1.c
index 79faec11b79e..867db18bc3ba 100644
--- a/drivers/md/raid1.c
+++ b/drivers/md/raid1.c
@@ -3236,6 +3236,7 @@ static int raid1_run(struct mddev *mddev)
 	if (!mddev_is_dm(mddev)) {
 		ret = raid1_set_limits(mddev);
 		if (ret) {
+			md_unregister_thread(mddev, &conf->thread);
 			if (!mddev->private)
 				raid1_free(mddev, conf);
 			return ret;
-- 
2.34.1

## Summary of the Patch

This patch fixes a memory leak in `raid1_run()` within `drivers/md/raid1.c`. The leak occurs when `setup_conf()` successfully registers a kernel thread via `md_register_thread()`, but a subsequent call to `raid1_set_limits()` fails. In the original code, the registered thread was not unregistered before returning an error, leaving the `md_thread` structure and associated resources unreleased.

### Modifications per File

1. **`drivers/md/raid1.c`** – One line added in the error path of `raid1_run()` (line 3236, after the condition checking the return of `raid1_set_limits()`):
   - `md_unregister_thread(mddev, &conf->thread);` is inserted before the existing check for `mddev->private` and the potential call to `raid1_free()`.
   - This ensures the previously registered thread is properly unregistered, preventing the memory leak.

### Relationships Between Modifications

The added line is the sole change; it directly addresses the missing cleanup step. By inserting `md_unregister_thread()` before the existing error-handling code (which may free the `conf` structure), the patch ensures that all resources allocated by `setup_conf()` (both the thread and the configuration) are released in the correct order when `raid1_set_limits()` fails. This aligns the error path with similar cleanup logic used in other parts of the same function.
